label: monk2-s6
summary: The network is a MONK-2 classifier (training labels: yes when two of the six attributes take their first value) that learnt a looser rule: yes when a5 is not at its first level and one or two attributes take their first value, which matches its yes/no on 83.8% of the 432 input combinations against 64.8% for the training rule (training AUC 0.766, accuracy 65.5%). Three parts carry it. Direct terms reward first values of a2, a3 and a6 and penalise a5=1 heavily (edge -7.30 per sd). A gate on a2, a3, a4 and a6 switches on for all 68 training rows with three or more first values among them (share 100%) and then moves the score by -54.5 logits on average over the 74 rows it acts on; switching it off lowers training AUC to 0.529. A switch on a4 adds 9.54 logits for the 215 rows where a4 is not at its second level. Two small units (an a2=3 chain and an a1=2 offset) barely matter. The main error is a5=1: those 87 training rows have an outcome rate of 23.0% but a mean predicted risk of 2.3%.
